def:finite-interface.title: Finite classical Einstein--Standard-Model interface
def:finite-interface.note: Partial: RegulatedSMConfiguration/explicitRegulatedStandardModelAction encode a finite link/vertex Standard-Model configuration with the four-term (Euclidean) matter action of (I2)-(I4), and sm_group proves the quotient presentation S(U(3)xU(2)) = (SU(3)xSU(2)xU(1))/Z_6 of eq:gauge-group ; missing: the Lorentzian carrier and coframe variables (I1), the common gravity+matter action with its relative normalization (I4, gravity part), the positive source geometry (I5), and any single structure bundling (I1)-(I5).
def:finite-interface.plan: Write a Lean structure FiniteInterface bundling: a finite-dimensional real vector space Q_h (configuration chart), a differentiable common action S_h = S_g + S_SM : Q_h -> R (fields for both pieces plus the relative normalization constant), a coefficient bank record theta, the finite Dirac/Yukawa incidence operator, and a positive-definite Gram on the retained variation directions (I5). Reuse RenewalGeometry/StandardModel/ExplicitRegulatedStandardModelActionExact.lean:RegulatedSMConfiguration / explicitRegulatedStandardModelAction for the matter part and SMGroup.lean:sm_group for (I2). Missing: the Lorentzian carrier/coframe fields (I1) can only be carried as an abstract field (a coframe map plus an oriented signature predicate, cf. Lorentz/Reconstruction.lean:MarkedDiracDatum) since no manifold reconstruction exists; the gravity action must be an abstract differentiable functional. Definition only, no theorem.

prop:renewal-interface.title: Renewal realization of the finite interface
prop:renewal-interface.note: Partial: the companion finite Standard-Model structural packet (gauge quotient, generation rank, weak doublet, finite Dirac incidence) is assembled as the typed certificate finiteStandardModel_sourceNative_emergence ; missing: a Lean finite-interface structure and a proof that the companion constructions instantiate (I1)-(I5), in particular the Lorentzian carrier and common-action normalization.
prop:renewal-interface.plan: Requires the structure of def:finite-interface plus a proof that the companion Lean packets instantiate every field. The matter side is available (StandardModel/FiniteStandardModelSourceNativeEmergenceExact.lean:finiteStandardModel_sourceNative_emergence, ExplicitRegulatedStandardModelActionExact.lean), but no Lean object supplies a Lorentzian carrier with coframe variables on a comparison cylinder or a common gravity+matter action with the physical relative normalization; the gravity companion files (Gravity/FiniteLineValuedEinstein.lean, Gravity/FiniteBRSTWardEinstein.lean) are line-valued abstract actions, not a coframe action. Needs reformulation: either weaken (I1)/(I4) to abstract fields (then it becomes a medium assembly) or build the missing carrier, which is research-level.

def:tests.title: Physical variation space
def:tests.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: test space, C^{r_0} norm, compactly supported variation tuple, determining core, metric lift; nothing in NCG/ encodes the physical variation space of smooth compactly supported tuples on a spin cylinder.
def:tests.plan: Presupposes smooth compactly supported sections of Sym^2 TM, T^*M (x) ad P and matter bundles over a spin cylinder with a C^{r_0} norm in an atlas and its completion. Mathlib has smooth manifolds/vector bundles and ContMDiff but no C^r norms on sections, no compactly supported section spaces, and no bundle metrics; nothing in the library encodes them. A faithful definition needs that infrastructure; a chart-local surrogate (compactly supported C^r maps R^4 -> R^N with the sup of derivative norms, via Mathlib iteratedFDeriv) would be medium but changes the statement.

def:regulator.title: A finite-interface regulator sequence
def:regulator.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: regulator sequence, reconstruction map, test lift, first-variation consistency c_h(K), stationarity eps_h(K); Flagship/EinsteinHandoff.lean only carries an abstract sequence x : N -> X with a scalar defect, not the reconstruction/test-lift data of this definition.
def:regulator.plan: Depends on def:finite-interface, def:tests and reconstruction maps R_h into smooth local fields on M; c_h(K) and eps_h(K) are suprema over the C^{r_0} unit ball of differences of Frechet derivatives. Missing: the test space (def:tests), a Lean notion of reconstructed smooth field on bundles over M, and the linear test lifts I_h. Gravity/EinsteinHandoff.lean only has an abstract sequence with a scalar defect. Could be stated abstractly (test space = arbitrary normed space V, I_h : V -> T Q_h linear, R_h : Q_h -> Z with Z a normed field space, c_h/eps_h as operator-norm suprema) as a medium definition, but that is a reformulation.

prop:source-bound.title: Scaled source control of physical stationarity
prop:source-bound.note: Partial: gt_protected_riesz proves the Gram Cauchy-Schwarz bound <Lu,v>^2 <= <u,Lu><v,Lv> for a range source e = Lu on a real inner-product space, i.e. |a[w]| <= ||a||_{G^{-1}} ||w||_G ; missing: the assembly eps_h(K) <= L_h sqrt(R_h) + e_h with the test-lift bound ||v_h(v)||_G <= L_h ||v|| and the identification error e_h.
prop:source-bound.plan: Pure finite-dimensional Cauchy-Schwarz assembly. State on a real inner-product space with a positive-definite Gram G (or its induced inner product): from |a[w]| <= ||a||_{G^{-1}} ||w||_G (RenewalGeometry/Certificates/GTProtectedRiesz.lean:gt_protected_riesz gives the range-source form <Lu,v>^2 <= <u,Lu><v,Lv>), the lift bound ||v_h(v)||_G <= L_h ||v||, and the identification error e_h ||v||, derive sup_{||v||<=1} |D S_h[I_h v]| <= L_h sqrt(R_h) + e_h. Only the triangle inequality, Real.sqrt monotonicity and csSup/iSup bound are needed; define eps_h as an iSup over the unit ball of an abstract normed test space.

prop:native-consistency.title: Growing-band consistency of the unchanged finite action
prop:native-consistency.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: growing-band consistency, Cartan plaquette curvature, Euler density E_0, stencil Taylor expansion h K^3.
prop:native-consistency.plan: Consistency of the full lattice Euler row of S_h^loc (eq:native-densities, Cartan+YM+Higgs+Dirac plaquettes with logarithms) against the continuum Einstein-Standard-Model Euler density E_0 with error h K^3. Requires formalizing the local action (see lem:native-scaling), the continuum Euler density including the Levi-Civita/spin-connection chain, and multivariate Taylor expansion of stencils with uniform constants. Nothing beyond DiscreteAnalysis/UniformFiniteDifferenceRemainderExact.lean (first-order remainders) and CovariantPlaquetteExpansion.lean (unshifted plaquette) exists; the continuum Euler density is not defined anywhere. Research-level infrastructure.

thm:native-source.title: Leakage-tolerant physical forcing estimate
thm:native-source.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: leakage-tolerant forcing, physical residual R_B R_D, tau_{h,m}, forcing budget F_{h,k}, logarithmic factor.
thm:native-source.plan: Needs Sobolev norms L^2_t H^k_x on a slab, the trigonometric reconstruction I_h^trig, the physical residual maps R_B, R_D, lem:native-tail-transfer, lem:log-source-upgrade (holomorphic strip / contour shift) and prop:native-consistency. None of these objects exist in Mathlib or the library (no Sobolev spaces, no Paley-Wiener decay, no continuum Euler rows). Hard by every ingredient.

thm:native-closure.title: Quantitative finite-action stability and Einstein--Standard-Model closure
thm:native-closure.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: actual-jet state, C_t H^k stability, Riem convergence, stress convergence, first-exit bootstrap, D^{full}.
thm:native-closure.plan: Composition of thm:native-source with the symmetric-hyperbolic actual-jet stability estimate prop:coupled-bootstrap (H^k energy estimates, commutator estimates, Gronwall, first-exit bootstrap on T^3) and the algebraic stress identification. Requires Sobolev spaces on T^3, Kato-type energy estimates for symmetric hyperbolic systems and curvature/stress algebra; all absent. Research-level.

cor:native-rate.title: An explicit cofinal rate
cor:native-rate.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: cofinal rate, dyadic summability, K_h ~ h^{-beta}, h^{1-beta(k+4)}.
cor:native-rate.plan: The conclusion inherits thm:native-closure, so the corollary as stated is hard. The self-contained part, F_{h,k} = O(h^{1-beta(k+4)} (1+|log h|)^{k+1}) and eps^phys = O(h^{1-3 beta}) from sigma_h=O(h), K_h ~ h^{-beta}, the tail rates eq:native-tail-rate and the definitions eq:native-forcing-budget, plus dyadic summability of h_n^rho (1+n)^{k+1}, is an easy real-asymptotics lemma (Asymptotics.IsBigO, Real.log bounds, summable_geometric) and could be split off and proved in a day.

thm:source-selection.title: Same-record selection from the actual signed action drift
thm:source-selection.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: stopped action drift, legal-edge mask, telescoping subprobability masses, Markov inequality selection score, exit probability.
thm:source-selection.plan: Finite-state, finite-horizon probability. Model: Fintype state X, sub-stochastic legal kernels K_j (nonneg rows summing to <= 1; cf. MarkovChains/FiniteMarkovHeatKernel.lean RowStochastic/EntrywiseNonnegative), surviving masses mu_{j+1} = mu_j K_j, actions a_h : X -> [A^-, A^+]. Prove (i) the telescoping identity sum_j sum_x mu_j(x) d_{h,j}(x) = sum_x mu_J(x) a(x) - a(x_0) - (killed mass credited at last legal value) >= -D_h^A, hence eq:source-slope-occupation from the drift inequality; (ii) build the finite path measure of the stopped chain (product of kernels on Fin (J+1) -> X, a Finset-weighted PMF) and apply Markov's inequality to the mean score to get eq:source-selection-failure. Missing: the finite path-measure construction with killing and the deterministic min-score argument; all finite sums, several days.

prop:native-reader.title: Exact native-energy to physical-tail certificate
prop:native-reader.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: affine reader, weighted high-frequency coefficient map, kernel condition T ker Q = 0, Moore-Penrose square root pinv, weighted ell^1 duality.
prop:native-reader.plan: Finite-dimensional linear algebra. State with H_src = EuclideanSpace R n, Q positive semidefinite (Matrix.PosSemidef), T : H_src -> (block index -> R^d) linear, weight w_l > 0, and tau as the weighted block-l^1 norm. Prove: a constant c with sum_l w_l ||T_l xi|| <= c <xi,Q xi>^{1/2} for all xi exists iff T (ker Q) = 0 (necessity: kernel vectors have zero energy; sufficiency: restrict to (ker Q)^perp where Q is definite, finite-dimensional norm equivalence). The optimal-constant formula needs Q^{dagger/2}: build it from Analysis/HermitianMoorePenroseInverse.lean:hermitianMoorePenroseInverse combined with Matrix.PosSemidef.sqrt (or diagonalize once via Matrix.IsHermitian.spectral_theorem) and then it is the operator norm of T Q^{dagger/2} from l^2 to weighted l^1 (a finite sup). Affine offset by triangle inequality.

cor:native-reader-sobolev.title: Sobolev positive-form reader criterion
cor:native-reader-sobolev.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: Sobolev positive-form reader, diagonal multiplier (1+|l|^2)^{1/2}, dyadic shell count O(R^4), K^{2-q} tail.
cor:native-reader-sobolev.plan: Two finite pieces: (a) from R^* L^{2q} R <= C_R Q and ||u_soft||_{H^q} <= C_R deduce ||u_h(x)||_{H^q} <= C(1+sqrt V) with H^q the weighted l^2 norm sum (1+|l|^2)^q |u_hat(l)|^2 on the finite mode set, a Loewner-order inequality on finite matrices (easy); (b) the lattice-sum bound A_{N,K,m,q}^2 = sum_{K<|l|_inf<=N} (1+|l|_1/K)^{2m} (1+|l|_2^2)^{-q} <= C K^{4-2q} for q > m+2, via dyadic shells in Z^4 with O(R^4) points (needs a counting lemma #{l in Z^4 : |l|_inf <= R} <= (2R+1)^4 and comparisons |l|_1 <= 4|l|_inf, |l|_2 >= |l|_inf) and Cauchy-Schwarz (Parseval on the finite Fourier index set). Missing: the shell-counting/geometric-sum estimate and the identification of tau_{h,j} with the weighted l^1 tail; all finite sums, several days. Sharpness clause optional.

thm:native-selected-closure.title: Same-source selected finite-action Einstein--Standard-Model closure
thm:native-selected-closure.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: same-source selected closure, selected record, Borel-Cantelli, summable adjacent differences.
thm:native-selected-closure.plan: Assembles thm:source-selection, the reader bound and thm:native-source/thm:native-closure; inherits the Sobolev/PDE stability machinery of the latter. The Borel-Cantelli summability clause (MeasureTheory.measure_limsup_eq_zero) is medium on its own, but the closure bound eq:selected-closure is research-level.

cor:selected-polynomial.title: An explicit polynomial selected-source regime
cor:selected-polynomial.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: polynomial selected-source regime, exponent window, failure probability O(h^{2a}+h^{2eps}).
cor:selected-polynomial.plan: Inherits thm:native-selected-closure. The exponent arithmetic in app:native-polynomial-proof (failure probability O(h^{2a}+h^{2eps}) from the five terms, the order of the terms in bar F_{h,k}, and the resulting rho) is an easy standalone real-asymptotics lemma; the closure statement itself is hard.

cor:gauge-robust-reader.title: Gauge-robust weak-sector reader entrance
cor:gauge-robust-reader.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: covariant jet energy, discrete Kato inequality, algebraic Higgs frame, causal temporal gauge, logarithmic link coordinates, full covector gauge invariance.
cor:gauge-robust-reader.plan: Requires the discrete Kato inequality, discrete Sobolev inequalities on a periodic grid with link-independent constants, finite-difference chain rules for the normalized Higgs frame, causal temporal gauge with discrete Gronwall, a discrete-symbol Parseval bound giving an all-mode H^q bound, plus the finite Ward identity for the full action covector. Individual pieces (Kato: |delta|F|| <= |D^U F| from the reverse triangle inequality and unitarity; gauge covariance of the covector) are medium, but the discrete Sobolev embeddings on grids in d<=4 with uniform constants do not exist in Mathlib or the library (DiscreteAnalysis/OperationalSobolevWeylExact.lean is unrelated). Overall hard.

thm:prefix-stationarity.title: Alternative finite-prefix stationarity criterion
thm:prefix-stationarity.note: Partial: descent_upper proves the Taylor descent inequality f(a+v) <= f(a) + <grad f(a),v> + (Lambda/2)||v||^2 used in eq:prefix-descent1, and bregman_floor the strong-convexity floor (m/2)||v||^2 <= D_Psi used for the potential Psi_h ; missing: the balance residual b_j, the telescoped prefix average eq:prefix-average with the h^{-2} Hessian-scale constants, and the selected-slope conclusion eq:prefix-selected (the legacy file instead treats a stationary law of an accepted kernel).
thm:prefix-stationarity.plan: Finite-dimensional descent calculation on an inner-product space E (the mass norm). Take eq:prefix-Fisher and eq:prefix-Hessian as hypotheses (Hessian bound as a Lipschitz bound on the gradient: ||grad A(x)-grad A(y)|| <= K_0 h^{-2}||x-y||, strong convexity of Psi as (grad Psi(y)-grad Psi(x), y-x) >= g_* ||y-x||^2 and Lipschitz g^*). Reuse RenewalGeometry/Action/AcceptedBregmanStationarityExact.lean:descent_upper (Taylor descent inequality eq:prefix-descent1) and bregman_floor; then the algebra of app:prefix-stationarity (Young's inequality, E(x) = b_j - upsilon^{-1}(p(y)-p(x)) + (E(x)-E(y)), squaring, summing, telescoping A(theta_0)-A(theta_J) <= D_0, taking the min of a finite list) is elementary Finset.sum manipulation. Missing: only this assembly with explicit constants C_0, D_1; the file's later stationary-law material is not needed.

cor:prefix-table.title: Finite-table certification for the prefix-balance entrance
cor:prefix-table.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: finite-table certification, safe set, exit probability, balance sum, Markov inequality, dyadic Borel-Cantelli.
cor:prefix-table.plan: Needs a finite-horizon path measure for the tabled transitions (same construction as thm:source-selection), the pathwise inequality of thm:prefix-stationarity on the safe event G, Markov's inequality (MeasureTheory.mul_meas_ge_le_lintegral) to get eq:prefix-table-probability, and the first Borel-Cantelli lemma (MeasureTheory.measure_limsup_eq_zero) along a dyadic cutoff family on a common probability space. Missing: the path measure with safe-set indicator and the Markov step; several days once thm:prefix-stationarity is done.

cor:generated-nonempty.title: Nonemptiness of the controlled finite class
cor:generated-nonempty.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: spectral-midpoint evolution, constrained initial class, N^{-p}+tau rate, Dirac residual.
cor:generated-nonempty.plan: Restates thm:generated-dynamics (spectral Galerkin + midpoint recursion for a symmetric hyperbolic system with H^q energy estimates, constrained initial data via elliptic solvers). Requires Sobolev spaces on T^3, discrete energy identities and the coupled actual-jet system; none available. Hard.

lem:screen.title: Common compact screen
lem:screen.note: screen_strong_convergence proves the first assertion on a complex Hilbert space for N-indexed sequences: bounded Z_n weakly convergent, ||S_{h,R} - S_R|| -> 0, uniform tail exhaustion, S_R Z -> Z, with compactness of S_R rendered as complete continuity (bounded weakly convergent inputs have strongly convergent images, equivalent for compact operators on Hilbert space) and the norm bound sup ||Z_n|| < infinity spelled out explicitly (automatic from weak convergence). The whitened clause is strong_convergence_transfer: uniformly bounded, strongly convergent B_n = A_h^{-1/2} applied to the strongly convergent whitened packet gives Y_h -> Y; the Loewner bounds mI <= A_h <= MI enter only through that uniform bound.

prop:time-compactness.title: From spatial screens to spacetime compactness
prop:time-compactness.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: Aubin-Lions, Simon, finite-rank projections P_R, H^1(0,T) time regularity, precompact in L^2_t H; Grand/DiscreteAubinLionsResponseExact.lean only computes a sqrt time modulus from an interpolation and a negative-norm estimate and does not prove precompactness.
prop:time-compactness.plan: Requires precompactness in L^2(0,T;H) (Bochner space) from finite-rank spatial projections plus H^1(0,T) bounds on projected components: needs the one-dimensional Rellich compactness H^1(0,T) into L^2(0,T) (Arzela-Ascoli via Mathlib's BoundedContinuousFunction.arzela_ascoli is reachable, but the H^1 -> Holder-1/2 step and Bochner L^2_t H are not set up) and a total-boundedness/epsilon-net argument in L^2_t H. The abstract epsilon-net step (tail uniformly small + projected sequence precompact => precompact) is medium and could be proved on an abstract Hilbert space with OperatorLimits/L2BlockDiagonalCompactness.lean-style screens; the time-Sobolev compactness is the hard part. No Aubin-Lions in Mathlib.

prop:orlicz.title: A local quartic compactness certificate
prop:orlicz.note: Partial: integral_norm_sub_tendsto_zero proves the Vitali step (uniform integrability + convergence in measure implies L^1 convergence of the norm) on a finite reference cylinder ; missing: the superlinear-Phi (de la Vallee-Poussin) uniform integrability of |H_h|^4, Rellich compactness giving convergence in measure, and the L^4(K) conclusion.
prop:orlicz.plan: The Vitali step is available (RenewalGeometry/Continuum/GaussianKernelVitaliExact.lean:integral_norm_sub_tendsto_zero) and the de la Vallee-Poussin uniform integrability of |H_h|^4 from sup int Phi(|H_h|^4) < inf is a medium measure-theory lemma (MeasureTheory.UnifIntegrable). What is missing and hard is Rellich compactness H^1(K) -> L^2(K) on a bounded 4D region giving convergence in measure: no Sobolev spaces or Rellich theorem in Mathlib. If Rellich (convergence in measure of H_h) is taken as a hypothesis, the remainder is medium.

prop:sobolev-bosonic.title: A-priori Sobolev bounds imply bosonic strong compactness
prop:sobolev-bosonic.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: Rellich-Kondrachov, H^{2+sigma} into H^1, L^{4+delta} embedding, curvature convergence dA + A wedge A.
prop:sobolev-bosonic.plan: Requires Rellich-Kondrachov compact embeddings H^{2+sigma} -> H^1 -> L^4 and H^{2+sigma} -> C^0 in four dimensions, plus product continuity for dA + A wedge A. Sobolev spaces and their compact embeddings do not exist in Mathlib; only the abstract bilinear-diagonal lemma (Continuum/StrongInterpolationConvergenceExact.lean:tendsto_diagonal_bilinear) is available for the curvature step. Hard.

prop:dirac-stability.title: Lorentzian Dirac stability produces spinor $H^1$ compactness
prop:dirac-stability.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: symmetric hyperbolic, Dirac energy inequality, Gronwall, C_t L^2 Cauchy, H^1 interpolation; the only Gronwall lemmas (Gravity/GrowthComparison, Grand/FastFeedback, Grand/HypocoerciveScreensExact) are scalar Volterra/discrete forms unrelated to spinor systems.
prop:dirac-stability.plan: Symmetric-hyperbolic L^2 energy inequality for first-order systems with W^{1,inf} coefficients, Gronwall, H^1/H^2 interpolation on a closed 3-manifold and Cauchy-in-H^1 conclusion. No hyperbolic PDE energy estimates, Sobolev spaces on manifolds, or distributional limits of first-order systems exist in Mathlib/the library (Gronwall lemmas in Gravity/GrowthComparison and Grand/* are scalar). Hard.

def:compactness-certificate.title: Classical compactness certificate
def:compactness-certificate.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: compactness certificate (C1)-(C5), compact screen, Orlicz condition, spinor route (C4a)/(C4b).
def:compactness-certificate.plan: Presupposes L^inf/H^1/L^4/L^2 norms of bundle-valued fields on compact regions, compact screens (available abstractly: OperatorLimits/SMSTPositiveScreenExact.lean) and Orlicz integrals. H^1 of coframes/spinors and precompactness in L^4(K) of connections need Sobolev spaces; a purely abstract surrogate (a family of normed spaces with predicates) would be medium but not faithful.

def:strong-packet.title: Classical strong packet
def:strong-packet.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: strong packet, L^infty cap H^1 coframe convergence, L^4 connection convergence, H^1 spinor convergence, coefficient bank.
def:strong-packet.plan: Same obstruction as def:compactness-certificate: the packet is convergence in L^inf cap H^1, L^4, L^2 of curvature F_A = dA + A wedge A, D_A H, and H^1 of spinors on compact K. Needs Sobolev/weak-derivative infrastructure and bundle-valued L^p on manifolds. Abstract version (a tuple of normed spaces with a distinguished continuous curvature map) is medium.

thm:certificate-packet.title: Finite certificates produce the classical strong packet
thm:certificate-packet.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: diagonal extraction over bundle atlas, identification of curvature limit, Rellich, Orlicz; no field-level compactness assembly exists.
thm:certificate-packet.plan: Assembly of diagonal extraction, lem:screen (proved), prop:orlicz, prop:dirac-stability, Rellich compactness and distributional identification dA_h = F_{A_h} - A_h wedge A_h. Every non-abstract ingredient (Rellich, distributions on charts, weak derivatives, Sobolev spaces) is missing. The abstract skeleton (screens on Hilbert packets + diagonal subsequence extraction over a countable exhaustion, cf. OperatorLimits/VaryingHilbertWeakSubsequenceCompactness.lean and TopologicalDiagonalTendsto.lean) is medium but does not reach the theorem.

lem:products.title: Local product and coefficient continuity
lem:products.note: Partial: continuity of bounded bilinear maps under strong (and strong x bounded-weak) convergence is proved on abstract normed spaces ; missing: the Holder instantiation L^p x L^q -> L^r, the explicit quadratic bound eq:quadratic-product, the algebraic coefficient convergence on the coframe chart, and the spin-connection convergence eq:spin-connection-convergence.
lem:products.plan: The first clause (L^p x L^q -> L^r product continuity and the quadratic bound eq:quadratic-product) is medium: Mathlib's Holder inequality for eLpNorm (MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_smul_le_mul_eLpNorm / Memℒp.mul with 1/p+1/q=1/r) plus one-factor-at-a-time telescoping, and the abstract bilinear versions already exist in Continuum/StrongInterpolationConvergenceExact.lean:tendsto_diagonal_bilinear and Continuum/WeakStrongBilinearPairingExact.lean. The coefficient clause (smooth algebraic functions of e_h, e_h^{-1} converge in L^inf cap H^1) and eq:spin-connection-convergence require the chain rule for weak derivatives of compositions in H^1 and the Levi-Civita/spin-connection formula; Sobolev spaces are absent, so these clauses are hard. Split: prove the L^p clauses first.

prop:variation-continuity.title: First-variation continuity from primitive fields
prop:variation-continuity.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: first-variation continuity, dual C^{r_0} norm, Yang-Mills/Higgs/Dirac-Yukawa/gravity sector estimates, Palatini first-order density.
prop:variation-continuity.plan: Sectorwise Lipschitz estimate of the full first variation of the Einstein-Standard-Model action in the dual C^{r_0} norm with respect to d_K; needs the continuum action on bundle-valued Sobolev/L^p fields, the Palatini first-order density, spin connections, and the dual test norm. None of the field-level objects exist. Research/infrastructure-level.

thm:main-limit.title: General subsequential Einstein--Standard-Model variational closure
thm:main-limit.note: Partial: one_sequence_limit/einstein_extension prove the abstract skeleton (sequence in a compact container, continuous residual bounded by vanishing defects, hence a subsequence converging to a zero-residual point), and conditional_local_weak_Einstein_matter_handoff derives the limiting scalar Euler and 2chi(G+Lambda g)=T identities from assumed sectorwise convergence of finite first variations plus vanishing defects (essentially uniqueness of limits) ; missing: compactness derived from the certificate, first-variation continuity in the strong-packet topology, the source-bound residual estimate eq:main-residual-bound, and the concrete Einstein-Standard-Model field equations.
thm:main-limit.plan: The abstract skeleton is in place (Gravity/EinsteinHandoff.lean:one_sequence_limit, einstein_extension; Gravity/ConditionalLocalWeakEinsteinMatterHandoffExact.lean:conditional_local_weak_Einstein_matter_handoff) and eq:main-residual-bound is a triangle-inequality assembly of prop:source-bound (easy), c_h and prop:variation-continuity. What is missing and hard: thm:certificate-packet (compactness), prop:variation-continuity, and the concrete distributional Einstein-Standard-Model equations. An abstract conditional version (compactness + continuity + vanishing residual => stationary limit) is essentially already proved; the theorem as stated is hard.

prop:cofinal-transport.title: Summable cofinal transport
prop:cofinal-transport.note: Partial: summable adjacent distances give a Cauchy sequence and a limit in a complete normed space (positive_outcomes_converge, tendsto_of_summable_dist), and cofinal_transport_attribution adds uniqueness of the limit in a finite weighted norm ; missing: the componentwise d_K packet, identification of the curvature and covariant-derivative limits, and the two-route direct-comparison clause.
prop:cofinal-transport.plan: Abstract form: d_K is a finite sum of norms of differences in complete normed spaces (one per packet component) plus |theta_h - theta|; summable adjacent distances give Cauchy sequences and limits (Continuum/ThreadCutoffCompactnessExact.lean:tendsto_of_summable_dist, Measurement/TrineCofinalCompleteScreenExact.lean:positive_outcomes_converge, Predictive/PredictiveRecordBatch00.lean:cofinal_transport_attribution for uniqueness). Missing: the componentwise packaging (a Fintype-indexed family of complete normed spaces with the sum metric; summability of the sum implies each component summable), the two-route comparison clause (two sequences with dist tending to zero have equal limits: tendsto_nhds_unique), and the identification clause stated abstractly as: the limit of a convergent sequence that also has a subsequential limit z equals z. The curvature identification is inherited from thm:certificate-packet and should be kept as a hypothesis. Several days.

cor:cofinal-unique.title: Cofinal uniqueness and route independence
cor:cofinal-unique.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: cofinal uniqueness, route independence, strong-packet limit identified as Einstein-Standard-Model solution; only the abstract summable-Cauchy ingredients cited under prop:cofinal-transport exist, and the legacy thm:GT-cofinal-route-independence is itself conditional_interface.
cor:cofinal-unique.plan: Composition of prop:cofinal-transport (medium) with thm:main-limit (hard). Abstractly (uniqueness of limit + limit is stationary) it is easy once thm:main-limit is available as a hypothesis, but as stated it inherits thm:main-limit.

thm:regular-branch.title: Regularity criterion for variational closure

prop:monotonicity.title: A sufficient Euclidean defect-removal mechanism
prop:monotonicity.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: strongly monotone operator, coercive Euclidean Higgs operator, weak-to-strong V cap L^4.
prop:monotonicity.plan: Abstract Hilbert-space monotone-operator argument. State: V real Hilbert space with a second norm ||.||_4 (continuous embedding), A_h : V -> V' (or V -> V via Riesz) satisfying the strong monotonicity inequality, H_h weakly convergent to H (WeaklyConverges as in OperatorLimits/VaryingHilbertWeakStrongPairing.lean, or Mathlib's WeakSpace), A_h(H_h) = J_h -> J and A_h(H) -> J strongly in V'. Then <J_h - A_h(H), H_h - H> -> 0 by strong-times-bounded-weak pairing (Continuum/WeakStrongBilinearPairingExact.lean:tendsto_of_strong_of_bounded_weak; boundedness of weakly convergent sequences via Banach-Steinhaus), so c_1||H_h-H||_V^2 + c_2||H_h-H||_4^4 -> 0. Missing: only the assembly with a dual-space formulation; the 'covariant H^1 norm' clause should be read as V's norm. Several days.

thm:hyperbolic.title: Common-slab metric stability
thm:hyperbolic.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: common-slab metric stability, reduced wave equation, H^{s-2} algebra, differentiated wave energy, L^1_t source, Riem convergence.
thm:hyperbolic.plan: Quasilinear wave-equation energy estimates on [0,T] x Sigma with H^{s-1} x H^{s-2} differences, Sobolev algebra/product estimates, commutator bounds, Gronwall with L^1-in-time sources, and the curvature formula. prop:subsidiary.title: Subsidiary equation and constraint stability
prop:subsidiary.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: harmonic gauge covector, subsidiary wave equation, contracted Bianchi, constraint energy estimate; Arithmetic/EinsteinClosure.lean and Flagship/EinsteinHandoff.lean mention Bianchi only as a displayed Noether identity.
prop:subsidiary.plan: Two parts: the algebraic identity eq:subsidiary from contracted Bianchi and the commutation formula 2 nabla^mu nabla_(mu C_nu) - nabla_nu nabla^alpha C_alpha = Box C_nu + Ric C (medium if a coordinate curvature framework with Bianchi identities existed; Gravity/CoordinateCurvature.lean has coordinate Christoffel/curvature but no covariant-derivative calculus or Bianchi identity), and the one-form wave energy estimate with Gronwall (hard, same obstruction as thm:hyperbolic). Overall hard.

prop:smooth-sampling.title: Smooth sampling is a consistency realization
prop:smooth-sampling.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: smooth sampling consistency O(h), strong packet convergence of reconstruction.
prop:smooth-sampling.plan: Depends on prop:mesh-consistency (hard) and prop:variation-continuity (hard) through the triangle inequality; the inequality eps_h <= c_h + C_K d_K itself is easy given those. As stated hard.

prop:critical-shadowing.title: Nondegenerate critical-point shadowing
prop:critical-shadowing.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: Newton shadowing, frozen-Newton contraction, uniformly invertible linearized Euler map; the only ContractingWith uses (Grand/RenewalStateTransportCompleteMetricExact.lean) concern state transport, not a Newton map.
prop:critical-shadowing.plan: Self-contained finite-dimensional frozen-Newton contraction. State on a finite-dimensional (or complete) normed space X with F : X -> X, B = (DF(x0))^{-1} with ||B|| <= M, DF Lipschitz with constant L on a ball, ||F(x0)|| <= C_0 h. Show T(x) = x - B F(x) maps the closed ball of radius rho = 2 M C_0 h into itself and is a contraction with constant M L rho < 1/2 for small h (mean-value inequality Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasFDerivWithin_le applied to x -> x - B F(x), whose derivative is B(DF(x0) - DF(x))), then Mathlib's ContractingWith.exists_fixedPoint on the complete ball; conclude F(x*) = 0 and the reconstruction bound from the Lipschitz hypothesis (S4). Missing: everything but Mathlib primitives; no library file has this Newton argument (ContractingWith appears only in Grand/RenewalStateTransportCompleteMetricExact.lean for state transport). The final 'd_K(R_h x*, z_*) = O(h)' clause needs prop:smooth-sampling and should be kept as a hypothesis.

prop:homogeneous.title: A nonvacuum Einstein--Higgs comparison family
prop:homogeneous.note: Partial: curved_einstein_00 computes the FLRW Einstein component G_00 = 3((adot/a)^2 + k/a^2), the left side of the Friedmann constraint eq:Friedmann-initial at k=0 ; missing: the Einstein-Higgs ODE system eq:homogeneous-ODE, local existence with a>0, constraint propagation, and verification of the remaining Einstein/Higgs/gauge equations.
prop:homogeneous.plan: Finite ODE + algebra. (i) Local existence for the smooth 4-dimensional system eq:homogeneous-ODE: Mathlib's IsPicardLindelof.exists_forall_hasDerivAt_Ioo_eq gives a C^1 local solution (smoothness needs an extra bootstrap; state C^1 or C^2 and note it). (ii) a(t) = a_0 exp(int H) > 0 from the first equation (uniqueness for the linear ODE). (iii) Constraint propagation: the derivative of 3H^2 - Lambda - kappa(pi^2/2 + U) vanishes along solutions (HasDerivAt algebra, a few lines). (iv) Einstein equations on flat FLRW with a homogeneous scalar: reuse RenewalGeometry/Gravity/CurvedFLRW.lean:curved_einstein_00 (G_00 at k=0 gives 3H^2) and curved_ricci_spatial/curved_scalar to get G_ij = -(2 addot/a + H^2) a^2 delta_ij, and match with the Higgs stress rho = pi^2/2 + U, p = pi^2/2 - U from eq:H-stress. Missing: the G_ij component from the existing Ricci lemmas and the explicit stress tensor of the homogeneous scalar; the gauge-current/fermion clauses are trivial with A = 0, Psi = 0 but require a Lean statement of those equations (state them explicitly for this ansatz). Several days.

lem:Whitney.title: Commuting reconstruction and positive comparison norm
lem:Whitney.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: Whitney form, de Rham map, commuting coboundary, mass matrix, projection convergence; only the Loomis-Whitney inequality (Grand/AtlasIsoperimetry.lean) exists, which is unrelated.
lem:Whitney.plan: Whitney forms on a shape-regular simplicial mesh, the de Rham map, R_h W_h = I and d W_h = W_h d_h need simplicial complexes with barycentric coordinates and differential forms on simplices; Mathlib has neither simplicial differential forms nor Stokes on simplices, and the library's only Whitney hit is the Loomis-Whitney inequality. The mass-matrix positivity and strong convergence of projections also need L^2 forms. Hard infrastructure.

prop:mesh-consistency.title: Smooth local action consistency
prop:mesh-consistency.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: parallel transport Taylor expansion, plaquette holonomy I + h^2 F + O(h^3), Riemann-sum quadrature error, differentiated transport.

Continuum fields, transport ODEs and quadrature on regions are all missing. Hard.

prop:weak-palatini.title: Weak-curvature Palatini passage
prop:weak-palatini.note: Partial: the L^2-L^6 Holder interpolation to L^q for 2 < q < 6 (with the p > 3/2 exponent arithmetic) is proved concretely at eLpNorm level, and the passage strong coframe -> strong wedge product -> pairing with norm-bounded weakly convergent curvature, plus the four-linear volume-density limit, are proved on abstract normed spaces with the interpolation bound as hypothesis ; missing: the instantiation on L^p(K) fields (Holder boundedness of the wedge L^{2p'} x L^{2p'} -> L^{p'}, weak L^p as weak-space convergence), the coframe-variation clause, and the connection-Euler pairing caveat.
prop:weak-palatini.plan: Most of the abstract passage is proved (Continuum/FiniteMeasureL2L6InterpolationExact.lean L2-L6 interpolation; Gravity/PalatiniWeakStrongLimitExact.lean curvature_pairing_tendsto_of_coframe_interpolation, palatini_and_holst_pairings_tendsto; Gravity/PalatiniDeterminantVolumeExact.lean). Missing: instantiating on Lp(K) fields: the Holder wedge bound ||e_h wedge e_h - e wedge e||_{p'} <= C ||e_h - e||_{2p'}(...) via Mathlib's eLpNorm Holder inequality (MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_smul_le_mul_eLpNorm / Memℒp.mul) for a bounded bilinear pointwise map, weak L^p convergence of R_h rendered as convergence in the weak topology of Lp (dual pairing with L^{p'}, WeakSpace or a hypothesis 'for all test in L^{p'} the integral converges'), and the coframe-variation clause (same argument with one factor a variation). The connection-Euler caveat is a hypothesis. Several days of Lp bookkeeping.

prop:improvement.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: nonminimal xi |H|^2 R, improvement tensor, W^{2,p} weak metric convergence, assembled distributional limit.
prop:improvement.plan: Distributional limit of f_h G(g_h) + (g Box - nabla nabla) f_h with g_h weakly convergent in W^{2,p} and strongly in W^{1,inf}: needs Sobolev spaces W^{2,p}, weak convergence in them, the coordinate Einstein tensor as linear-in-second-derivatives plus quadratic first-derivative terms (Gravity/CoordinateCurvature.lean has the algebra but only for smooth coordinate functions), and integration by parts against tests. Hard.

lem:half-ricci.title: Twisted half-Ricci contraction
lem:half-ricci.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: Clifford contraction, half-Ricci identity, first Bianchi, twisted curvature.
lem:half-ricci.plan: Purely algebraic identity in a Clifford algebra with a curvature tensor satisfying antisymmetry and the first Bianchi identity. State: c_a in a Clifford algebra (Mathlib CliffordAlgebra with quadratic form eta, or explicit 4x4 gamma matrices) with c_a c_b + c_b c_a = -2 eta_ab, R_{abcd} a real tensor with R_{abcd} = -R_{bacd} = -R_{abdc} and the cyclic identity, R^S_{ab} = (1/4) sum R_{abcd} c^c c^d, Ric_ab = sum_c eps_c R_{cacb}; prove sum_b eps_b c_b R^S_{ba} = (1/2) sum_b eps_b Ric_ab c_b using the triple-product decomposition c_b c_c c_d = c_[b c_c c_d] - eta_bc c_d + eta_bd c_c - eta_cd c_b and Bianchi. Missing: everything (no curvature tensor structure with Bianchi identity in the library; Lorentz/AnchorClifford.lean has gamma matrices but no curvature). With explicit Fin 4 sums and Matrix gamma matrices this is a finite computation (Finset.sum over Fin 4, heavy but decidable after ring normalization); the twisting term is additive bookkeeping. Several days.

prop:spinor-prolongation.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: tangential spinor prolongation, commuted Dirac operator, normal jet algebraic relation.

Nothing of this scale exists. Hard.

prop:coupled-bootstrap.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: coupled actual-jet stability, commutator estimate, H^k algebra, first-exit bootstrap.
prop:coupled-bootstrap.plan: Symmetric-hyperbolic H^k energy estimate on T^3 with commutator estimates (Kato-Ponce type), Sobolev algebra for k > 3/2, Gronwall and first-exit bootstrap, then curvature/stress recovery. prop:generated-initial.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: conformal method, Lichnerowicz equation, L_* = -8 Delta + mu_*, Banach contraction, Gauss and vector constraints.

The contraction skeleton is medium (ContractingWith on a ball), but the Sobolev spaces, Laplacian isomorphism and constraint equations are missing. Hard.

lem:generated-physical-identification.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: analytic germ, Cauchy-Kovalevskaya, symmetric system uniqueness, Sobolev limit identification.
lem:generated-physical-identification.plan: Cauchy-Kovalevskaya analytic germs for the Einstein-Standard-Model Cauchy problem, uniqueness for symmetric hyperbolic systems, and Sobolev-limit identification. None available. Hard.

lem:native-plaquette.title: Regularity of the plaquette map
lem:native-plaquette.note: Partial: for the unshifted case a = b = 0 the four-exponential plaquette equals 1 + h^2 [X,Y] + O(h^3) in a Banach algebra, with an explicit cubic bound under contraction hypotheses ; missing: the shifted arguments a, b, the logarithm quotient Phi(h) = h^{-2} log(...), its analytic extension through h = 0 with Phi(0) = a - b + [X,Y], and uniform bounds on parameter derivatives.
lem:native-plaquette.plan: Extend RenewalGeometry/DiscreteAnalysis/CovariantPlaquetteExpansion.lean (norm_plaquette_sub_secondOrder_le, plaquette_sub_secondOrder_isBigO_right handle a = b = 0) to shifted arguments: the product e^{hX} e^{h(Y+ha)} e^{-h(X+hb)} e^{-hY} = 1 + h^2(a - b + [X,Y]) + O(h^3) follows from the same Banach-algebra exp expansion (Analysis/ExponentialTaylorRemainder.lean, GroupCommutatorBound.lean) with the two extra linear-in-h^2 terms; that part is a routine extension. The analytic-continuation clause needs a logarithm on a Banach algebra near 1 (not in Mathlib): define log(1+z) = sum (-1)^{n+1} z^n / n as a FormalMultilinearSeries with radius 1, get analyticity of h -> log(P(h)) from AnalyticAt.comp, and show the removable quotient h^{-2} log P(h) is analytic at 0 by factoring the power series of P(h) - 1 (its h^0 and h^1 coefficients vanish). Uniform derivative bounds on compact parameter sets follow from power-series coefficient bounds. Several days, mostly the Banach-algebra log.

lem:native-scaling.title: Differential-order scaling
lem:native-scaling.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: amplitude-preserving rescaling xi = Kx, rho = hK, nu = 1/K, K^2 bosonic and K Dirac stencil factors.
lem:native-scaling.plan: Exact algebraic identity once the local action eq:native-densities is defined in Lean (a large but finite definition over a periodic Z^4 grid: coframe e, jets q via delta_h^+, the Cartan reader eq:native-LC-reader, exponentials and plaquette logarithms using the Banach-algebra log of lem:native-plaquette, Higgs links and spin differences). The scaling statement is then: substituting y(x) = ytilde(Kx) turns delta_h^+ into K delta_rho^+, omega_h = K omegatilde_rho, exp(h omega_h) = exp(rho omegatilde_rho), F^h = K Ftilde (via the removable quotient of lem:native-plaquette with arguments nu A), K^h = K Ktilde, so each bosonic density factors K^2 and the Dirac density K; uniform regularity of the normalized stencils on compact sets is inherited from smoothness of the finite composition. Missing: the entire action definition and the substitution lemma; no continuum analysis. Several days to a week, mechanical.

lem:native-tail-transfer.title: Finite-order tail bounds
lem:native-tail-transfer.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: finite Fourier tail derivative bounds, |l^alpha| <= K^{|alpha|}(1+|l|_1/K)^j, mean-value Euler-row tail transfer.
lem:native-tail-transfer.plan: The first display (derivative bounds on trigonometric tails: |l^alpha| <= K^{|alpha|}(1+|l|_1/K)^j, finite Fourier sum bounded by tau_{h,j}) is medium: finite sums over the mode set with Complex.exp derivatives (Mathlib fourier/ZMod machinery, DiscreteAnalysis/LatticePeriodicDifferentiationExact.lean for periodic derivatives). The Euler-row transfer eq:native-Euler-tail (mean-value theorem for the finite Euler row as a smooth function of shifted jets; needs lem:native-firstjet-normal-form and lem:native-action-Hessian-type bounds) is medium. The L^2_t H^k_x source-tail bound eq:native-source-tail needs the continuum residual maps R_B, R_D and Sobolev norms, which are missing; that clause makes the lemma hard as stated.

lem:log-source-upgrade.title: Logarithmic derivative upgrade for a band-limited source
lem:log-source-upgrade.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: holomorphic strip a/K, contour shift, Plancherel low/high frequency split, logarithmic factor.
lem:log-source-upgrade.plan: Requires Fourier coefficients of a function holomorphic in a strip to decay exponentially (contour shifting / Paley-Wiener in three variables on T^3) and Plancherel for L^2_t H^j_x. Mathlib has Fourier series on AddCircle with Plancherel (tsum_sq_fourierCoeff) but no strip-holomorphy decay estimate for several variables; the frequency-split optimization once the decay is known is medium. Hard because of the complex-analytic step.

prop:native-rounding.title: A sufficient nodal-accuracy condition
prop:native-rounding.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: nodal rounding tolerance, discrete Parseval, O(h^{-4}) modes, (hK)^{-j} weight bound.
prop:native-rounding.plan: Finite discrete Fourier analysis on (ZMod n)^4: Parseval for the normalized DFT (Mathlib's ZMod.dft has a Plancherel-type identity; extend to the 4-fold product or reprove via orthogonality of characters on a Fintype), Cauchy-Schwarz sum_l |ehat(l)| <= sqrt(#modes) (sum |ehat|^2)^{1/2} with #modes = n^4 = O(h^{-4}), and the pointwise weight bound (1+|l|_1/K)^j <= C_j (hK)^{-j} for |l|_inf <= (n-1)/2 (since |l|_1 <= 2(n-1) <= 4 pi / h). The band-limited part contributes nothing to the tail. Missing: the multidimensional DFT Parseval and the counting; all finite. Several days.

lem:native-firstjet-normal-form.title: Shifted-first-jet normal form of the unchanged local action
lem:native-firstjet-normal-form.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: shifted first-jet normal form, discrete summation by parts, exact lattice divergence, collar functional; Grand/BoundaryCorner.lean and Grand/OpenPathWassersteinDualityExact.lean use summation by parts in unrelated settings.
lem:native-firstjet-normal-form.plan: Exact finite summation-by-parts identity on the periodic grid: the discrete product rule eq:native-SBP (<C, delta^+ W> = -<delta^- C, W> + delta^-<C, T W>) is a one-line Finset telescoping (cf. DiscreteAnalysis/LatticePeriodicDifferentiationExact.lean, FlowDuality.lean for similar sums); eq:native-C-firstjet is the integral form of the mean value theorem for the smooth coefficient C (Mathlib intervalIntegral of a derivative). The substance is the exact decomposition of the Cartan plaquette logarithm R^h as 'discrete curl of the connection + regular function of shifted connections' (follows from lem:native-plaquette's removable-quotient form) and collecting the exact lattice divergence into the collar functional. Requires the full local action definition (lem:native-scaling). Mechanical but sizable; several days once the action exists.

lem:native-action-Hessian.title: Uniform upper Hessian scale of the local action
lem:native-action-Hessian.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: uniform upper Hessian scale K_0 h^{-2}, inverse estimate ||delta^+ u|| <= 2 h^{-1} ||u||, action oscillation bound.
lem:native-action-Hessian.plan: Given lem:native-firstjet-normal-form (action = h^4 sum of a smooth F^(1) of finitely many shifted values and first differences), the bilinear bound eq:action-Hessian-bilinear is Cauchy-Schwarz over the finite sum with uniformly bounded second derivatives of F^(1) on the compact chart; eq:action-Hessian-scale follows from the inverse estimate ||delta^+ u||_{0,h} <= 2 h^{-1} ||u||_{0,h} (triangle inequality on the shifted sum, a few lines) and translation invariance of the mass norm; eq:action-span is boundedness of the density times the fixed cell count h^4 #Q'_h <= vol. Missing: the general 'Hessian of h^4 sum F(shifted jets)' bound with a fixed number of shifts per node (a finite double-counting lemma), and the second-derivative characterization (use Mathlib's iteratedFDeriv or a HasFDerivAt of the gradient). Several days, no analysis beyond finite sums.
